title: Cohort-aware correlated anomaly detector for cost + latency with automated explainers
creator: Marco Hernandez
description: Problem: We surface a large volume of noisy anomalies on cost, latency, and throughput metrics that are not triageable by oncall and produce alert fatigue. Current detectors operate at the global metric level and miss cohort-specific regressions (e.g., a single customer or region driving P95 spikes) and correlated effects across cost and latency. Goal: build a lightweight streaming detector that (1) scores anomalies per cohort (customer, region, model-version, route), (2) identifies correlated cross-metric events (cost ↔ latency ↔ error rate), and (3) attaches a short automated explainer that suggests likely root causes (traffic spike, model rollout, infra degradation, quantization change). The detector must run in the console analytics pipeline (low-latency, <90s detection SLA after metric ingest) and integrate with existing alert routing (Slack + PagerDuty) and the Console UI incident drawer. Constraints: pipeline memory and egress cost must remain bounded (prefer reservoir sampling and sketching), privacy: do not send PII to external services, must be compatible with Dedicated and Private deployment telemetry hygiene. Success criteria: reduction in noisy global alerts by 40%, increase in actionable alerts routed to product-owners by 30%, median time-to-first-meaningful-hint <5 minutes after alert. Deliverables: streaming job + unit/integration tests, new alert payload schema (includes cohort, correlated metrics list, explainer bullets, snapshot link), Console drawer UI hook docs, runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming job deployed to staging and processing 100k events/min with <90s end-to-end detection latency
Alerts include cohort-id, top-3 correlated metrics, and at least one explainer hypothesis in natural language
False positive rate evaluated on historical 6-month dataset shows >=40% reduction vs baseline global detector
Alert routing follows existing PD/Slack targets and populates Console incident drawer links
Docs and runbook updated; oncall walk-through completed with SRE and product owner
comments: 2025-01-17 - Marco Hernandez: Kickoff meeting notes: align on cohorts (customerId, region, route, modelVersion). Minimum viable cohorts: customerId (hashed), region, modelVersion. Avoid storing raw customer identifiers in analytics tiers.

2025-01-22 - Aisha Patel: Prototype in Flink using seasonal-trend decomposition (STL) + robust z-score per cohort. Early results: P95 noise reduced, but small cohorts produce high variance — proposing adaptive smoothing and cohort bucketing (min 50 events/window).

2025-01-30 - Data Eng review (Liam O'Connor): Recommended switching from per-cohort full-state to count-min sketches + reservoir samples for snapshots to keep state compact. Also suggested backfill test against 3 months of historical ingestion in staging.

2025-02-03 - PM review (Janelle Kim): Added acceptance criteria to require explainer text and Console drawer link. Prioritizing customer-impact cohorts for initial rollout: top 50 customers by spend and top 3 regions.

2025-02-05 - Aisha Patel: Implemented correlated-event detection: compute pairwise mutual information between metrics per cohort using rolling windows; thresholds tuned on historical ramp events. Pushed branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-analytics/pull/812
2025-02-05 - SRE comment (Priya Shah): Need to include circuit-breaker — if detection job lags >3x wall time, fallback to aggregated global detector to avoid missing alerts. Added as follow-up task.
2025-02-05 - Aisha Patel: Next steps: finalize explainer templates, wire alert payload to Console webhook, schedule canary for top-50 customer cohort for two weeks.
